context_needed: BRAC Ultra Poor Graduation (UPG) programme for ultra-poor youth aged 18-35 in Luweero and Masindi districts, Uganda (pp. 7-10). Quasi-experimental: 1,216 programme households and 865 comparison households matched by propensity score (Methodology, p. 10). Rounds: baseline 2017 and endline 2019 (pp. 14-15); 'Round' is the endline dummy and 'Treated' the programme-group dummy. Outcomes are shares of households (eats 2 or more meals a day; more than 2 income-generating activities; has savings), so coefficients are percentage points: the text on p. 18 reads 16.82 as a 17 pp impact and 33.02 as a 33 pp impact on savings.

stored_rows.outcome: > 2 meals (eats 2 or more meals a day)
stored_rows.note: percentage points. The header says > 2 meals but Table 7 (p. 18) defines the indicator as eats 2 or more meals.
percentage points. The Constant in this column (131.22) exceeds 100, which is impossible for a percentage; the DiD is stored as printed and matches the text (33 pp, p. 18).

not_stored.reason: group dummy: the baseline gap between programme and comparison households, not an effect
time dummy: change in the comparison group between rounds, not an effect

not_stored.cell: Observations, R2, Adjusted R2, Residual Std. Error, F Statistic

rule: In a regression DiD, only the programme interaction term (here Treatment*Round, bold in the table) is a programme effect. The group dummy, the round dummy, the constant and any covariate or fixed-effect rows are never stored.
